oneLiner: The only US-owned leading-edge logic maker, now growing again on server CPUs. The market is not paying for 2027 earnings; it is betting that Intel Foundry lands an external anchor customer and that a 2028-2030 earnings base several times today's is reachable.

verdict.stance: Cautious - right story, price ahead of it
verdict.summary: The operating turnaround is real: Data Center is supply-limited, gross margin has recovered and the foundry loss is narrowing. But the Q4 guide steps down sharply on PC memory costs, the share count is up ~17% in a year, and the multiple prices a foundry outcome that has no named high-volume customer yet. On our numbers the probability-weighted value sits below the live price, because the base case needs a mid-40s multiple on 2027 EPS just to hold. Two things would turn us positive: a named high-volume external 14A or 18A-P customer, and Xeon supply easing fast enough that Data Center growth outruns the PC slump in H1 2027.
wtb: FY2027 revenue of at least ~$68B (about +10% on a ~$62B FY2026) while the PC market stays soft through at least H1 2027.
Non-GAAP gross margin climbs back above ~42% by Q2 2027 after the ~38% Q4 2026 trough.
A named, high-volume external 14A or 18A-P customer is announced before 14A risk production in 2027.
The diluted share count stops growing: no new equity raise in 2027, holding near ~5.4B.

bear.why: Memory-driven PC weakness lasts all of 2027, substrate limits cap Xeon, and revenue is flat on FY2026. Non-GAAP net margin stays ~9% as 18A ramp costs and the foundry loss absorb the gains. With no anchor customer the market stops paying for 2030 foundry economics and the multiple falls toward that of a stalled turnaround.

base.why: Data Center keeps compounding as substrate supply eases from mid-2027 and the PC market recovers in H2; revenue +10% and non-GAAP net margin ~14% as the foundry loss narrows below ~$1.5B a quarter. Foundry customer interest stays unnamed, so the market keeps a high but no longer expanding multiple.

bull.why: Xeon supply unlocks, PC demand normalises by mid-2027 and a named high-volume 14A customer signs; revenue +23% and non-GAAP net margin ~19%. A visible path to foundry break-even lets the market capitalise 2028-2029 earnings, so the multiple stays at 50x.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 revenue assumes Q1 $13.6B + Q2 $16.1B + Q3 $16.5B + Q4 guide midpoint $15.5B = ~$61.7B. EPS = revenue x non-GAAP net margin / ~5.4B diluted shares (Q3 2026 diluted weighted average 5.307B plus stock comp): bear $60B x 9% = $1.00, base $68B x 14% = $1.76, bull $76B x 19% = $2.67. EPS is on a non-GAAP basis (excludes escrowed-share and equity-investment marks). Multiples apply to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Does the foundry earn the multiple, or is this a CPU recovery priced like a foundry?
debates.bull: 18A is shipping in Intel's own client and server parts, the 14A 0.9 PDK went out in October as committed, Socionext picked 18A-P in August, and press reports (unverified) link Apple to 18A-P for 2027.
debates.bear: The reverse DCF needs ~20% a year of earnings growth for a decade against revenue that shrank ~6% a year over the last three fiscal years. Foundry still lost $1.9B in Q3 and Intel no longer breaks out external revenue; Socionext is not a volume anchor.
debates.view: This is the debate that sets the multiple (32x vs 50x). Without a named high-volume customer before 14A risk production, the base case is generous. We would move to Neutral or Positive on a named volume commitment, not on 'inbound interest'.

signpost.metric: Named external 14A or 18A-P customer with stated volume or prepayment
signpost.threshold: positive if a top-10 fabless or hyperscaler commits; negative if 14A risk production starts with internal products only
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report (late Jan 2027, est.) through 14A risk production in 2027

debates.q: Can Data Center outrun the PC slump in H1 2027?
debates.bull: DCAI grew 78% in Q3 with 41% segment margin and demand Intel calls extraordinary; Nvidia systems pairing GPUs with Xeon add a new demand channel.
debates.bear: Output is capped by substrates, AMD's 192-core Turin parts have no direct Intel match, and CCPG fell 5% with management expecting PC weakness at least through H1 2027 as DRAM and NAND prices raise system costs. The Q4 guide is the first step down.
debates.view: The Q4 guide shows PC losses outweighing Data Center gains for now. The base case needs DCAI back to sequential growth by Q2 2027; if total revenue is still below $16B in Q2 2027, the bear case is in play.

signpost.metric: DCAI revenue growth and total revenue vs the $15.0-16.0B Q4 guide; Q1 2027 guide
signpost.threshold: positive if Q1 2027 revenue is guided at or above $15B with DCAI growing sequentially; negative if Q1 is guided below $14B

debates.q: How much of the per-share story survives dilution and accounting noise?
debates.bull: Q3 adjusted free cash flow was positive ($1.6B) as capex fell to ~$4.2B, and trailing operating cash flow is ~$14.9B through Q2 2026 despite GAAP losses; the equity raises bought fab capacity, not losses.
debates.bear: Diluted shares rose ~17% in a year (~5.31B in Q3 2026 vs ~4.53B in Q3 2025) after the government, Nvidia, SoftBank and the ~$23B public offering. GAAP net income ($3.3B) exceeded operating income ($2.5B) in Q3 on a $1.0B escrowed-share gain and $0.3B of equity gains, and these marks swing results in both directions.
debates.view: Value the company on non-GAAP EPS per diluted share and on cash flow, not on GAAP. Dilution is in the model at ~5.4B shares; another raise in 2027 would cut every scenario by its size.

signpost.metric: Diluted share count and adjusted free cash flow
signpost.threshold: red flag if shares rise above ~5.5B or adjusted FCF turns negative for two quarters
signpost.when: Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 reports (Jan and Apr 2027, est.)

thesis: Server CPUs are supply-limited, not demand-limited. Data Center was the strongest growth in 15 years per the CFO, and the constraint is substrates, which is a timing problem rather than a share problem.
Margins have structurally reset higher. Q3 non-GAAP gross margin of 44.1% compares with 40.0% a year earlier, as better 18A yields and cycle times reduce wafer costs.
The foundry loss is narrowing. The Q3 operating loss of $1.9B compares with $2.3B a year earlier on 58% higher segment revenue, and the 14A PDK milestone was met on time.
Strategic shareholders underwrite the balance sheet. The US government, Nvidia, SoftBank and the public offering together fund the 18A/14A buildout and make failure politically expensive.
risks: Dilution has already taxed the turnaround. Shares are up ~17% in a year (debate 3); the per-share value of any recovery is smaller, and the 14A buildout could need more capital.

The price needs a better business than the record shows. The reverse DCF bar is ~20% a year of earnings growth vs a shrinking three-year revenue base; a foundry miss compresses the multiple, not just EPS.
PC memory squeeze. Higher DRAM and NAND prices shrink the PC market into at least H1 2027, and CCPG is still about half of revenue.
GAAP results are noisy. Escrowed-share and investment marks moved GAAP EPS from -$2.16 in Q2 to $0.60 in Q3; GAAP net income above operating income is not operating profit.
Competitive gaps remain. AMD leads at the top of the server core-count range and Intel has no material merchant AI accelerator revenue.
catalysts: Early Nov 2026: AMD Q3 2026 report - server CPU share read vs Intel's substrate-limited Xeon (debate 2).
Late Jan 2027 (est.): Q4 2026 report - delivery vs the $15.0-16.0B guide, Q1 2027 guide, share count and adjusted FCF (debates 2 and 3).
Through 2027: named external 14A or 18A-P customer announcements; the Apple 18A-P report remains unverified (debate 1).
2027: Intel 14A risk production (internal products first) - whether an external customer is on it (debate 1).
H1 2027: DRAM and NAND contract pricing - the swing factor for PC demand (debate 2).

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 2026; reported Oct 29, 2026)
points: Revenue $16.5B, +21% YoY, above the $15.8-16.8B guide midpoint; DCAI $7.3B +78%, CCPG $8.1B -5%, Foundry $6.7B +58% (including intersegment).
Non-GAAP gross margin 44.1% (GAAP 43.0%); non-GAAP operating margin 19.6% (GAAP 15.3%).
Non-GAAP EPS $0.52 vs a $0.38 guide; GAAP EPS $0.60, including a $1.0B escrowed-share gain.
Segment operating income: DCAI $3.0B, CCPG $2.3B, Foundry -$1.9B.
Operating cash flow $5.1B, gross capex $4.2B, adjusted free cash flow $1.6B; diluted shares 5.31B.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 29). Revenue $16.5B, +21% YoY and ahead of guide, carried by Data Center: DCAI $7.3B (+78%) at a ~41% segment margin, with purpose-built silicon revenue more than doubling. Client (now CCPG, Client Computing and Physical AI) fell 5% to $8.1B as memory prices raised PC system costs. Foundry revenue rose 58% to $6.7B, mostly internal, and its operating loss narrowed to $1.9B. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 beat the $0.38 guide; GAAP EPS of $0.60 was lifted by a $1.0B escrowed-share gain and $0.3B of equity gains. Adjusted free cash flow turned positive at $1.6B. During the quarter Intel completed a ~$23B public equity offering and agreed to acquire Classiq. Note: the filings data behind the charts runs through Q2 2026 and does not yet include this quarter.
guidanceProse: Q4 2026 guide: revenue $15.0-16.0B, non-GAAP gross margin 38.0% (GAAP 37.1%), non-GAAP EPS $0.25 (GAAP $0.10), non-GAAP tax rate 11%. That is a sequential step down in revenue, ~6pts of gross margin and roughly half the EPS. On the call management said PC weakness from DRAM and NAND pricing lasts at least through H1 2027, Xeon output is limited by substrate supply that will take time to ease, and 18A supply is being steered toward data center parts. On foundry, the 14A 0.9 PDK shipped in October; no new high-volume external customer was named, consistent with Lip-Bu Tan's policy of not naming customers.
segments: Data Center and AI (DCAI): $7.3B in Q3 2026 (+78% YoY), ~44% of revenue; Xeon 6 / Clearwater Forest on 18A, supply-limited by substrates.
Client Computing and Physical AI (CCPG, formerly CCG): $8.1B (-5% YoY), ~49% of revenue; Panther Lake on 18A, pressured by PC memory costs.
Intel Foundry: $6.7B (+58% YoY), mostly intersegment; operating loss $1.9B. External customers include Socionext on 18A-P (Aug 2026).
competitive: AMD leads at the top of the server range (192-core Turin) and keeps taking x86 share; Intel's answer is constrained by supply, not design.
TSMC remains the process and ecosystem benchmark; Intel Foundry must win external volume from a standing start.
Nvidia owns AI compute, but its $5B stake and GPU systems paired with Xeon made it a demand channel as well as a rival.
Arm-based PCs and hyperscaler Arm server CPUs shrink the x86 pool itself.
moat: The x86 installed base and OEM/enterprise relationships, scale as the only US-owned leading-edge logic manufacturer, and an explicit government and strategic-investor backstop. Process leadership is not restored: 18A closes much of the gap and 14A is on schedule, but TSMC keeps customer trust, and until a volume customer commits, the foundry moat is a hope rather than an asset.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: free cash flow is volatile through the 18A/14A buildout, so cash-flow valuation understates or overstates in any single year; the reverse DCF on forward EPS shows how much recovery is already priced.
